Strict Lean Discipline §6 bans `native_decide` used to mask an unproved structural claim but permits a genuinely decidable finite computation; this is the latter — `nontrivialBrunnian borromean`, `borromean.length = 6`, and `wordsBelow6.all (fun w => !nontrivialBrunnian w)` are a finite enumeration of 3-braid words with a Kauffman/TL₃ bracket evaluation each, which plain kernel `decide` would very likely not discharge in reasonable time. The caveat is the axiom footprint: `native_decide` adds `Lean.ofReduceBool`, so this theorem and everything downstream of it leaves the standard three-axiom set, and an `#print axioms` reader will see it. Advisory: keep, but record the footprint where the minimality result is cited, and prefer `decide` if the enumeration is ever narrowed.
